reviews.headline: Up 2.9% on day one, but it's all parked cash; 3 buy orders still waiting
reviews.markdown:
**Account:** $1,029.66 vs $1,000 start (+2.91% today and this week). The goal is +5%, so we're a little over halfway. The S&P buy-and-hold would be $1,009.40, so we're ahead by about $20. Be honest: no trade closed, so this gain is not from Patient Levels. It came from the account's moves in the market, and I can't tell you how much was luck.

**Core vs trading:** About $519 of idle cash was moved into the S&P (market order at 3:52pm, still pending). Settled cash is $30.91. No open positions, so no stops to report.

**Orders today (none filled yet):**
- TLN limit buys at $346.08 and $355.66. TLN closed near $365.61 (+9.8%), so both are sitting below the price. They only fill if it pulls back.
- BWXT limit buy at $115.83, with the stock at $115.86, so this one is very close.

**Agent decision:** BWXT jumped 6.7% on the Westinghouse AP1000 deal news. The desk took no action. That's right: news is priced in within minutes. Past BWXT deal headlines averaged -2.8% over the next 20 days. It's still down 51% from its 1-year high.

**Watch tomorrow:** whether the BWXT order fills, and whether TLN dips. TLN's insiders sold $23M over the year (COO sale on Nov 17). Nothing was bought, which is a mild caution.

**Lesson:** A good day isn't proof a strategy works. Patient Levels has only 1 data point so far, so judge it on many trades, not one.

reviews.headline: Down 1.24% today, but still +1.62% on the week and ahead of the S&P
reviews.markdown:
**Account:** $1,016.74 vs $1,000 start. Today -$12.92 (-1.24%). The week is +1.62%, short of the +5% goal (the goal isn't forced). The S&P buy-and-hold would be $1,004.23, so we're ahead by about $12.50, but we lost to the S&P today (-1.24% vs -0.48%).

**Why we fell:** Nuclear stocks dropped 2.49% as a group. Our "panic" holdings took the hits: LEU -4.94, VST -4.15, UUUU -2.13 (in the day's attribution), and the parked SPY -2.16. No Patient Levels trades were open, armed or waiting, and none closed today.

**Orders (all 15:40, still pending):**
- Sold $71 of parked SPY to fund a trade. This created a small wash-sale flag: a -$0.61 loss that is deferred, not lost.
- Three "sharp-drop rebound" buys: AMD, NNE, SMR.
- Ten "thanksgiving" buys, one in each lineup stock.

**Concerns:**
- The account shows cash of -$352.92 and settled cash of $0. With no margin allowed, 13 market buys pending on that is a red flag. The Account Officer and Risk Manager should confirm what will actually fill.
- The basket is below its 10-day average, so normal new buys should be blocked. These orders come from other rules, so someone should check that is intended.

**Red day verdict:** This looks like the cost of holding in a falling market (the S&P is below its 200-day average), not a broken rule. The cash question above is the possible fix. We shouldn't change any rule over one day.

**Watch tomorrow:** which orders fill and at what size, the cash balance, and UUUU (down 68% in a quarter, with law-firm "investigation" notices out). Those notices are noise, but they add to the pressure on the stock.

Cameco's Q3 (reported Oct 30) showed a C$2M adjusted loss after a longer Key Lake mill outage, and the US$1B at-the-market (ATM) share program was renewed and doubled in early December. The stock has since fallen about 25% in 20 days, partly on a sector-wide selloff in AI-linked nuclear names, so the news is already priced in.

A further sector slide would also hit CCJ, since it is below its 10-day, 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages and the basket is falling. The other risk is a sharp oversold bounce (RSI2 of 0.58) that stops out a patient buy. The next real catalyst is Q4 results and the 2027 production plan in February, and I couldn't confirm an exact date.

The share sale (which dilutes existing owners) is a real overhang, but the stock is far below its averages and the basket is falling, so I say no new buy for now and wait for a base to form.

From a plant standpoint, an AP1000 contract for BWXT Canada is a supplier award inside Westinghouse's reactor program, so it's real but slow: the actual revenue arrives over years of construction, not in the next few sessions. And BWXT's main business is US Navy reactors, so this is a small piece of its picture.
engineer.real_effect: Supplier work for AP1000 reactor builds (Westinghouse's design), which only convert to meaningful BWXT revenue as construction proceeds over several years. No immediate change to any plant's output.
engineer.why: I checked the plant and fleet data: no outage or power event touches BWXT, and the AP1000 contract is a multi-year supply item. The basket gate is closed and the story is aggregator-recycled, so there's no timely edge.

BWXT.reason: The AP1000 supplier award is a recycled headline (the desk's own deal note dates it Nov 24) with no stated dollar value, and revenue from it arrives over years, not days. BWXT is also below its 50-day and 200-day averages, the basket is under its 10-day average so no new buys are allowed, and past BWXT contract news averaged -2.8% over 20 days.

pm.plan_summary: No trade in BWXT. Stale, small, slow-payoff news, a downtrending stock, and the basket gate is closed.
pm.say: I agree with News Investigator and Plant Engineer: this is recycled news about slow, multi-year revenue, so it is not a reason to buy. BWXT is down about 16% in 20 days and under its 200-day average, the basket gate is shut, and past contract headlines did slightly worse than the basket afterward, so I'm skipping.
pm.why: I checked the deal history, the age of the headline, the trend and the basket gate. Every check pointed to no edge, so I'd rather not trade.

research_log.name: panic_day_rebound
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-20 PROMISING (not proven): buy at the close when the market (SPY) falls 2%+, the stock falls 3%+ and is 15%+ below its 20-day high (CCJ Nov 5 2026 type). 61 distinct days since 2019: hold 4 days +3.6% avg / +3.3% median, up 62%; hold 6 days +5.3% / +6.2%, up 70% (p=0.001 by day), positive every year. Risk: when the panic is the start of a crash (Feb-Mar 2020, May 2022) it loses 15-21% and stops don't help (gaps). Buying next morning instead of the close keeps much less (+0.9% over 2 days). ~23 variants tried, so treat as a candidate for paper testing. | 2026-11-20 filters tried (first vs repeat panic, market vs 200-day avg, market drawdown, size of market/stock drop; 10 more trials): none removes the crash days cleanly, splits are 4-15 days and flip between halves. Kept the simple rule; protection = size (15% each, 45% total, 3 names). Now trading on paper as strategy #2. | 2026-11-20 round 3 (25 more trials): which 3 to pick barely matters (deepest-under-high +6.0% vs biggest-drop +5.3%, noise); VIX 40+ days best (+9.3%, 85% up, n=13); SECTOR-only panics have no edge (+0.6%), it needs the whole market; fixed 6-day hold best avg, but sell at +10% close or day 6 = +5.0% avg, 72% up, worst -17.5% (vs -21.4%) and frees cash sooner -> adopted. Non-panic swings: best is -10% in 3 days in a calm market, +2.1% over 6d vs +1.0% for any day, steady in both halves (practice candidate only). | 2026-11-23 exits (3 trials, 153 trades on 61 days): sell at +10% on a CLOSE or day 6 = +5.8% avg (71% up) beats a resting +10% limit (+4.4%, 75% up), a +8% limit (+3.7%) and a give-back guard (+5.5%); both halves agree. Winners often run past +10%, so selling intraday cuts them. No change: keep the close rule, no stop (crash-day gaps go straight through stops). | 2026-11-23 sizing (5 trials, $1,000 compounded 2019-2026 incl. 2020 crash): 15%/45% -> $2,248 (10.8%/yr, worst drop -16.5%); 25%/75% -> $3,666 (17.9%, -26.8%); 33%/100% -> $5,023 (22.7%, -34.5%); 50%/100% -> $5,832 (25.0%, -45.2%); 100% one name -> $10,767 (35.1%, -45.5%, only 44 trades: rides on single picks). Every year positive at every size. Owner chose to compound harder: ADOPTED 33% each / 100% total on paper. Panic days are rare (75 of 1,985 sessions), so cash sits idle most days; 3-down-days as an idle-cash setup: +1.66% over 5d vs +0.84% any day, 55% up, too weak alone. | 2026-11-23 adaptive size (13 trials: VIX bands, SPY vs 200d, depth, stock drop; 2 size tables): VIX<25 +7.3% (77% up), VIX 25-40 +2-3% (weakest), VIX 40+ +11.7% (83%); stock -8%+ +7.9% vs -3-5% +3.7%. Steps 10/15/25/40/50% by VIX zone + stock drop: $1,000 -> $5,863 (25.1%/yr, worst drop -23.2%) vs flat 33% $5,018 (-34.5%). Gain is mostly in the older half (newer 1.62x vs 1.64x), so the main win is the smaller drawdown. Same data used to pick the bands: in-sample. ADOPTED with the PM allowed one step up/down after the team talks; each PM size call is scored vs the rule (pm_size_score). | 2026-11-23 intraday caps on top of the close rule (+15/+20/+25% resting sells): +5.2/+5.6/+5.8% vs +5.8% without; no gain, kept as is. Trades that touched +10% intraday but closed below (62 of 153): finished +10.7% avg, 92% up, 66% ended at +10% or more -> holding through that dip is right. | 2026-11-23 profit-lock stops (after a close at +5/+6/+8%, stop at 0/+2/+3%, gap fills at the open): avg +4.8 to +5.3% vs +5.8% without, worst trade unchanged (-27.9%: crash trades never go up first). Not adopted. | 2026-11-23 WIDER UNIVERSE (same rule, $20M+/day and $3+ filter, 0.1% cost, best 3 by depth): nuclear 10: 83 trades +3.45% avg 64% up (older -0.1, newer +6.9); ~74 related stocks: 183 trades +3.95% 66% up (older +2.5, newer +5.4), every year positive; combined 191 trades +3.96%. By group: new nuclear +8.3% (39), AI/data-center +4.3% (131), grid equipment +4.1% (90), mining +3.3% (89), nuclear utilities +2.7% (44), defense +1.6% (36), gas +1.0% (78, worst -62%), builders +0.5% (56). Compounding (adaptive size, cash idle): nuclear only $1,955 (8.9%/yr, -18.7%) vs nuclear first + related fill $2,782 (13.8%/yr, -26.3%). ADOPTED on paper: nuclear picks first, empty slots from the related list. Note: this test's liquidity filter is stricter than the first panic test, so absolute numbers are lower than the earlier 25%/yr; compare within the test.

research_log.name: open_order_timing
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-23 (13 nuclear stocks, hourly bars Dec 2023-Nov 2026, 9,158 stock-days): the first hour is weak on average (-0.2 to -0.3%) on every gap size except gap-downs of 2%+ (+0.3%, halves disagree). Its low sits 2-3% under the open. Limit buys 1-3% under the open: ~80% of first-hour fills trade at the limit again after 10:30 anyway, and the ~20% that only fill in the first hour are the best trades (+4.5% to +5.2% by the close). So waiting until 10:30 gets no better price and drops the best fills. Kept: orders go in at 9:31 after the open prints (setups the open already broke are dropped first). Not adopted: orders before the bell (they fill at the open even when the stock gaps through support).

research_log.name: support_vs_dipbuy_fills
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-23 (10 nuclear stocks, Dec 2023-Nov 2026 hourly for support buys, daily for the dip-buy; $1,000, 25% per trade, max 4 open). Paper-style fills (touch = filled): support buys with the falling-sector block +0.44%/trade -> $3,369 (52%/yr, worst drop -28%); simple 2% dip-buy, sell back at the anchor close or 10 days -> $9,376. Realistic fills (price must trade 0.3% through the order): support buys +0.15%/trade, halves +0.37/-0.07 -> $1,348 (11%/yr, -44%); dip-buy -> $3,036 (47%/yr, -46%). Placing the support order 0.8-1.6% above the level doesn't fix it (+0.14 to +0.19%/trade, newer half negative). The dip-buy over 2008-2026 with realistic fills and $5+ stocks: 6.7%/yr, worst drop -64%; on the uranium ETF URA (no survivor bias) it lost money (-4.3%/yr). Conclusions: (1) the support buys' paper edge mostly comes from fills that only touched the price; (2) the dip-buy only shone in the 2023-26 bull and on surviving stocks; neither adopted as an upgrade. Added an honest-fill check (fill_check) so the paper record shows P&L without touch-only fills.

research_log.name: night_round_55_2026_11_25
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-25 07:10. VM silent since 04:42 (missed the 05:42 and 06:42 saves; owner messaged 06:52). Causes I can rule in/out from here: the backfill child is small (~10 MB per 90-day chunk), the service has RestartSec=20 so a systemd start-limit is unlikely; most likely a call that never returned in the night cycle, or the machine itself. Added a hang guard to the daemon: a thread exits the process (systemd restarts it 20 s later, pulling the latest code first) if the main loop makes no progress for 90 minutes (config hang_restart_minutes). Takes effect after the next restart.

research_log.name: ops_2026_11_25_stuck_save
research_log.verdict: 2026-11-25 10:00. Root cause of the 04:42-09:38 silence: the VM's hourly save ran 'git pull --rebase' which stopped halfway (rebase-merge left behind), so every later pull and push failed ('[rejected]'), the page froze and no new code arrived; the bot itself kept running. Owner reset the VM 09:17 and cleared it by hand 09:38 (rebase --abort, reset to origin, kept the VM's state.json). Fix: the save now clears any half-finished rebase first and, if the rebase pull fails, aborts and merges with the VM's own files winning (-X ours); tested on a throwaway repo with a stuck rebase: cleared and pushed with the VM's state.json. Plus the 90-minute hang guard (07:08).

idea.why: Stops sit just under the zone, so a stock with wide hourly swings is more likely to tag the stop on noise before the level holds.

notebook.note: We tested whether jumpy stocks (hourly swings above 4%) hit our tight stops more often. Only 294 of 9,798 trades matched. Results went the wrong way in both halves and were not statistically meaningful (p=0.34). Too few trades and too much noise to conclude anything, so we are not changing how we use the stop.
notebook.next: Only revisit if we collect more trades in the high-volatility group. Otherwise, drop it.

idea.why: A gap-down fill into the level often means news is breaking the support, and our research says drift after bad news is more reliable, so the level may not hold.

idea.why: The learn report found Wednesday fills worse in both the older and newer halves of the data, so it needs a direct check on the full practice book before anyone trusts it.

notebook.note: We tested whether Wednesday fills do worse, as the learn report suggested. The effect flipped sign between halves (+0.087R older, -0.040R newer) with p=0.60, so it is likely noise. The learn report's pattern did not survive a check on the full practice book.

idea.why: If the whole sector group is below its 10-day average, a resting buy just above support is more likely to be in a sector-wide selloff that breaks the level, so these entries should do worse. This is distinct from the already-banned basket rule because it's measured per trade, not as a hard gate.

notebook.note: Tested whether resting buys made while the whole sector basket is below its 10-day average do worse. They did not do worse in the way I expected; the opposite held in both halves, with the older half much stronger than the newer. Rejected as a rule.
notebook.next: Log as rejected. Don't add a per-trade filter from this; the basket gate already exists as a hard rule.

idea.why: Stocks that already ran more than 10% in the five days before a buy are more likely to be chasing a spike that fades, so resting buys after big run-ups may underperform. Testable on the existing fill data.

notebook.note: Tested whether buys after a 10%+ five-day run-up underperform. Direction matched the claim in both halves but the difference is small and not statistically solid (p=0.16, 457 trades).
notebook.next: Log as rejected for now. If revisited, test against a pre-set threshold instead of one chosen after seeing results.

questions.question: TLN closed around $364 after a 9% day, yet the resting buy sits at $355.66 with a $354.24 support zone. Is this order still a deliberate plan, or should it be canceled now that the stock has moved well away from it?
questions.answer: The resting buy at $355.66 was a plan for a dip toward the $354.24 support, and TLN now trades about 2.4% above it after a 9% sector bounce, which our rules say not to chase. The basket is still below its 10-day average, which blocks new buys, so this order should not be left resting into a bounce. I agree with the Risk Manager's concern that a sharp reversal could fill it, and I'd cancel it rather than let it sit until the PJM capacity-auction delay is decided.

questions.question: Has the PJM December capacity-auction delay been decided? The Talen headline calls the long-term sales a 'pullback opportunity', but the earnings driver is still an open regulatory question.
questions.answer: I checked the desk files and the headlines we have for PJM. Nothing I can see shows the December capacity-auction delay has been decided; the only mention is the Talen 'pullback opportunity' article, which doesn't report a regulator decision. Since the earnings driver is still pending, I'd treat the 9% jump as pricing in an unresolved outcome, and I agree with the Risk Manager that the resting TLN buy shouldn't be left in place into this bounce.

questions.question: BWXT rallied 7.4% on the AP1000 demonstration-parts headline, but the price is still down about 8% on the month and 15% below its 20-day high. Does the $115.37 support zone mean anything after a news-driven spike, or is it just where the price happened to be before the pop?
questions.answer: The $115.37 zone was drawn before the news pop, and the price has since run 7.4% above the zone's level, so it's a stale level, not a fresh floor. Nothing in the desk's notes shows support forming after the headline, and the basket is still below its 10-day average, so no new buys are allowed anyway. I agree with the Risk Manager that the basket rule should block this, and I'd treat the BWXT setup as stale until the price actually retests a zone drawn from after the bounce.

questions.question: The AP1000 headline has no disclosed contract value, so is this news big enough to change BWXT's revenue outlook, or is it a small qualification step that the market is overpricing?
questions.answer: The AP1000 headline is a qualification step with no disclosed dollar value, and BWXT's own history shows contract-news pops tend to fade over 20 days (median -2.8%), so I don't think it changes the revenue outlook. I agree with the Level Analyst that the $115.37 zone predates the bounce and is stale, and the basket is below its 10-day average, so no new buy either way.

questions.question: Has anyone confirmed whether the PJM December capacity-auction delay has been decided? It is the main earnings driver for Talen, and the 'pullback opportunity' headline does not answer it.
questions.answer: I checked the desk files for the PJM December capacity-auction delay and found nothing confirming a decision. The only dated reference is the Nov 30 expiry on our TLN resting order, which falls before any known auction timing. Since TLN is about 2.9% above our buy level and the basket is below its 10-day average, the order should not sit live on an unresolved regulatory question.

questions.question: TLN's COO Brad Berryman sold about $19.8M of stock on Nov 17 at roughly $345-365. Is that a planned 10b5-1 sale or an open-market sale, and does it change how we read the insider picture?
questions.answer: Brad Berryman's Nov 17 sale is about $19.8M of TLN stock, but the desk files don't record whether it was a planned 10b5-1 sale or open-market, so I can't classify it from what we have. That matters because our rule treats open-market sales as meaningful, and TLN's yearly insider net is already -$23M. I agree with the Risk Manager that the TLN resting buy should be canceled given the basket rule and the unresolved PJM auction delay, and the insider question doesn't change that.

questions.question: Was the TLN COO's Nov 17 sale of about $19.8M a planned 10b5-1 sale or an open-market sale?
questions.answer: I checked the TLN COO's Nov 17 sale against the desk notes. The files show the trade as a $19.8M sale by Brad Berryman, but they do not say whether it was planned under a 10b5-1 plan or made in the open market. Without that detail I can't tell if it's the insider signal we weigh or routine noise, so I'm marking it unsure and asking for the Form 4 footnote.

questions.question: The PJM December 2029/30 capacity-auction delay request is the main earnings driver for Talen, and it has not been decided. How does the stock's 9.6% jump square with an open regulatory question that could go either way?
questions.answer: I checked whether the PJM December 2029/30 capacity-auction delay has been decided, and our files don't show a decision, so I can't tie the 9.6% TLN jump to a resolved outcome. The 'pullback opportunity' headline doesn't answer the regulatory question, and the market may be pricing a favorable result before it's final. I agree with the Questioner that this is worth tracking, though the order-cancel call belongs to the owner and the Risk Manager's rule.

questions.question: Has the PJM December 2029/30 capacity-auction delay request been decided? Talen's earnings depend on it, and nobody has confirmed it.
questions.answer: I checked the desk files and the news, and nothing I can find confirms whether the PJM December 2029/30 capacity-auction delay request has been decided. The Talen 'pullback opportunity' headline doesn't settle it, so this stays an open regulatory question that could move TLN either way. I agree with the Risk Manager that it's worth tracking, but I'm not treating the 9.6% jump as explained.

questions.question: Has the PJM December 2029/30 capacity-auction delay request been decided by FERC? If no ruling exists, what explains TLN's 9.6% jump on an unconfirmed regulatory question?
questions.answer: I checked the desk files and the market data for any FERC ruling on the PJM 2029/30 capacity-auction delay request and found none; the auction is still scheduled to close Dec 15 under the existing price collar, so I'm assuming it goes ahead unless a ruling appears. The 9.6% TLN jump is not explained by anything I can confirm, and I agree with the Questioner that it's an open regulatory question that could reverse either way. The basket gate is closed too, so no new buys regardless.

questions.question: The desk's notes show the nuclear basket gate is closed (below its 10-day average) and the market is fearful. Is there any setup on the list that should be placed while the gate is closed, or should we skip them all until it reopens?
questions.answer: The basket gate is closed right now (the nuclear group is below its 10-day average), and our rule blocks new buys in that case, so every setup on the list should be skipped until it reopens. I agree with the Macro Analyst and the Research Lead on this: the gate is the deciding factor, not any single chart. The Questioner's concern is real in that the gate status should be stated plainly before the Thanksgiving window, not assumed.

questions.question: The Kazatomprom corruption probe headlines keep coming, and CCJ is down 27% over the quarter. Has anyone checked whether the probe affects Kazakh uranium output, or is it just a governance story with no supply effect?
questions.answer: I checked the desk files. The Kazatomprom probe is an arrest of one executive and board member over alleged corruption, with the company saying it is cooperating; nothing in the sources reports lost output, mine shutdowns, or a change to guidance. Governance stories like this usually don't move supply, so I see no supply link to our stocks.

questions.question: TLN was up about 9.6% on a regulatory question with no ruling confirmed. Is the stock pricing in an expected outcome of the Dec 15 PJM auction, and if so, what does the pre-auction pattern in our notes say about holding into it?
questions.answer: I checked the PJM question. No FERC ruling on the delay request is in our files, the Dec 15 auction is still on the calendar, and the notes show the pre-auction pattern is weak: when the price went up, power stocks popped on release day and then gave it back over 20 sessions, so the bounce on an unconfirmed question looks like noise, not a priced-in outcome. Talen's insider sale was pre-planned, so it's no signal either. I'd keep the Dec 15 date on the calendar and not hold into it on the strength of this.

questions.question: Does the Thanksgiving run-up rule (buy the basket, sell Black Friday at 1 pm) get blocked by the basket gate, which is currently closed?
questions.answer: The Thanksgiving run-up is a seasonal trade, not a signal that depends on support levels, so the basket gate applies to new entries but I checked the rule itself: our files show the pre-Thanksgiving session is only mildly positive and the desk's own notes say to take no entries until the basket reclaims its 10-day average. Since the Wednesday-before-Thanksgiving edge is about +0.7% for the S&P and our basket has its own history, the open question is whether the chief's trade was actually placed into a closed gate, which I can't confirm from the live orders list (none resting).

questions.question: Given that LIVE_ORDERS_RIGHT_NOW is empty, are any of the setups discussed above (TLN, VST, CEG, DNN, UUUU) actually resting, or is every mention just analysis with nothing placed?
questions.answer: Checked the live orders list: it's empty, so nothing is resting right now. The TLN $355.66 buy and the DNN, UUUU, VST and CEG levels in the chat are analysis only, and the basket gate is closed, so none of them could be placed anyway. Anyone quoting those levels as exposure is working from stale information.

questions.question: LIVE_ORDERS_RIGHT_NOW is empty, so is the TLN buy at $355.66 actually resting, or was it only discussed? If it is resting, why was it not canceled after the basket gate closed?
questions.answer: I checked the live order list and it is empty: no resting orders exist, and every order is a day order that expires at its close. So the TLN buy at $355.66 was only discussed, not placed, and nothing can fill during the closed-gate session. The gate is still closed, so the right move is to confirm the order is not in the broker and stay flat on TLN.

questions.question: The PJM Dec 15 auction is on the calendar and no FERC ruling on the delay has been found. Should the desk treat that event as the main risk for TLN and VST through the window, and does any of our rule set account for it?
questions.answer: The desk's notes say the PJM Dec 15 auction is a known calendar event, and no FERC ruling on the delay has been found, so the auction is treated as going ahead. Our own history says the pop on auction results tends to fade (about -3% over 20 sessions after up-auctions), so for TLN and VST the auction is a reason to avoid adding or to trim into a pop, not a reason to buy. I agree with the Macro Analyst that the basket gate is closed right now, so no new buys in either name regardless.

questions.question: Nothing in our desk's notes explains how the nuclear basket lost ground through the quarter while the reactor fleet stayed about 89% running. Is the selloff about the AI-power trade unwinding, or is there a fact we are missing?
questions.answer: The nuclear basket's slide looks more like the AI-power trade unwinding than an operations problem: the reactor fleet is 89% running with only one long outage (Salem 1), and nothing in the news points to a plant-level fact that would explain a 17% quarterly drop in CEG. Our own notes say the power names kept falling even with normal operations, and the desk's research shows that's positioning, not news. Sentiment is what's driving these, so setups may take longer to work.

questions.question: Has anyone confirmed whether the PJM December 2029/30 capacity auction (Dec 15) is still on schedule? Talen's earnings depend on it, and the 9.6% jump on an unconfirmed ruling has not been explained.
questions.answer: I checked the desk files and found no confirmation that the PJM December 15 auction has been delayed or decided. The only delay request is unruled, so the auction should be assumed to go ahead on schedule, and the TLN and VST moves are being discussed as if the outcome were known. That makes this a real risk to watch, not something to trade on.

questions.question: Has the PJM 2029/30 capacity auction (scheduled to close Dec 15) been confirmed on schedule, or has the delay request been decided? No ruling has been found, yet TLN jumped 9.6% on the headline.
questions.answer: I checked the PJM 2029/30 auction question against the desk's notes. No FERC ruling on the delay request has been found as of Nov 25, so the Dec 15 auction should be treated as on schedule, and that makes it a real catalyst for TLN and VST. The 9.6% jump on an unconfirmed headline is the kind of move we should not chase. I agree with the Questioner that this is a risk to hold, not a setup to add to.

questions.question: Does the desk's Thanksgiving run-up rule get blocked by the closed basket gate, and would any of the open setups (TLN, VST, CEG) be affected by Black Friday's half-day weakness?
questions.answer: The Thanksgiving run-up rule is not blocked by the closed basket gate, because the gate only stops new buys and the desk's notes show no active Thanksgiving-window order to cancel. Black Friday weakness for the power names is a sentiment check, not a trade signal, so it does not change the open setups.

policy.item: US ban on Russian enriched uranium
policy.status: In force since Aug 11 2024 and lasts until the end of 2040. Waivers (exceptions) are only allowed until Jan 1 2028.
policy.why: Russia supplied about a fifth of the enriched uranium US reactors use. From 2028 that has to come from somewhere else.

policy.status: Centrus has waivers for all deliveries already promised to US customers in 2026 and 2027. Well over half of what it delivers through 2027 comes from Russia's Tenex.
policy.why: 2028 cuts both ways for Centrus: its cheap Russian supply ends, but demand for US-made enrichment rises.

policy.status: Since Nov 2024 Tenex needs a separate Russian export licence for each shipment to the US; extended through Dec 31 2027.
policy.why: Russia can stop shipments early at any time, which would hit Centrus before 2028.
